scope: Exact 44-line adapter-only change and active consumer/failure routing; no multi-frame scanner dispatch claim.

checks.result: SessionRouter requests one active timeframe per stock symbol and consumes adapter ohlc events. Existing native 1m event/callback remains unchanged. Higher requested timeframe is separately labeled and reaches runner candle storage and active-timeframe analysis.

Existing getCandles requests IEX bars with descending server order and sorts mapped numeric timestamps ascending. Added path retains provider start and sets end using requested interval; only end<=triggering native bar end is emitted. Last emitted provider start prevents duplicate delivery on later refreshes. No synthetic OHLC aggregation or invented minute-completeness rule.

One promise per subscription prevents overlapping refreshes. Completion, rejection and cleanup verify current subscription object identity; unsubscribing clears the map and resubscribing creates a fresh object, preventing late result publication to a replacement subscription.

Current-subscription REST rejection reaches existing stream-truth-unavailable event path, then OrderRouter broker-truth record and existing entry block. It is not a log-only catch. Obsolete subscription rejection does not publish the newly added unavailable event.

validation: Exact git-tree source/diff and reachable producer/consumer review only. Root behavioral proof and Mercury remain separate; no root executable config/state loading or production edits performed.
limitations: The two-bar refresh is not a general history-gap recovery protocol.
Delivery is driven by native bar arrivals and asynchronous provider REST availability.
This adds the one requested timeframe; it does not implement all-frame strategy dispatch.
